findings.title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` is silently ignored now that `.small-action` is a flex container
findings.body: This PR makes `.small-action` a flexbox container (`@include flexbox()` / `@include align-items(center)`). Per CSS, floats have no effect on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule inside `.small-action` stops working for any button that is a direct child of the `.small-action` row. Previously that button was pinned to the right edge of the post row; now it will be packed immediately after `.small-action-desc` on the left, because the container has no `justify-content: space-between` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. If the button is a direct child (as the old float-based layout implies), this is a visible layout regression for small action posts (e.g. undo/expand controls). Either keep the button out of the flex flow or replace the float with a flex-appropriate right-alignment (`margin-left: auto` on the button or `justify-content: space-between` on the container).

findings.title: `align-items` mixin omits `-moz-box-align`, so the `-moz-box` fallback gets no alignment
findings.body: The `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` mixins emit `display: -moz-box` / `display: -moz-inline-box` for old Gecko browsers, and the `order()` mixin emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but the new `align-items()` mixin only emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items` — there is no `-moz-box-align` line. Any browser that ends up using the `-moz-box` display fallback therefore gets the old box layout without the requested vertical alignment (e.g. the header `.contents` and `.small-action` rows will not be centered there). Either add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` to the mixin or drop the `-moz-box` display fallbacks so the mixin set is self-consistent.

findings.title: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property
findings.body: The `align-items()` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, but no Microsoft flexbox implementation ever supported that property — IE10's 2012 'tweener' syntax uses `-ms-flex-align` (which the mixin already emits on the previous line). The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code that no browser will parse; it should be removed to avoid implying IE coverage that doesn't exist.
